A day in the fight

How I stay in it.

No secret program. It mixes up, but this is the shape of it.

Early

Up

Up early. The day starts before the excuses do.

Every AM

Yoga

Every morning. The part people don’t expect. It keeps me loose, keeps me recovering and keeps me fighting.

2–3x a week

Strength

Strength and conditioning in the morning, 2 or 3 days a week. Stay strong.

Noon

Mix it up

When work allows: Muay Thai, boxing or MMA at lunch. It changes day to day.

PM

Fight

Muay Thai, jiu-jitsu or MMA in the evening. Pads, rolling, sparring, sweat.

Weekend

Play

BMX, rock climbing, some sparring, and whatever my boys want to do. That’s the real workout.

Train for the long fight

Keep fighting.

I never stopped. Fight, stay loose, recover, and show up again tomorrow. Not just to keep going, but to make it your best life.

Fight

Muay Thai, jiu-jitsu, MMA, karate. Sparring keeps you sharp, humble and honest. Every round shows you what to work on next.

Stay loose

Yoga every morning is my baseline. It keeps the body and mind flexible so I can keep fighting.

Live your best

It’s a mindset. Don’t just keep going. Make it the best life you can. Long live the fight.

The enlightened fight

Light becomes fight.

The word was ENLIGHTEN. Then the bolt came down and turned the L into an F. That’s ENFIGHTEN.

In the old traditions, the bolt is called the vajra. It means both thunderbolt and diamond. It strikes like lightning, it can’t be broken, and it cuts through illusion. Diamonds are made under pressure. So are fighters.

On the mat you get hit, you fail, you get back up. If you’re willing, it shapes you. Then you take that into life.

And the fight doesn’t end with you. You pass it on to everyone you train with, everyone you help. That’s how it lives.

Long live the fight.
